title: read response
description: Standard output of read in JSON mode: the workfile (READ-011), a node (READ-024), a property (READ-035), or a refusal. $defs/base is ReadResponse (overview 2.1).

base.description: ReadResponse: a Node or a ReadProperty.

overlay-property.description: A property of the workfile as written: no source.

overlay-node.description: A node of the workfile as written (READ-051). Every node has origin overlay.

overlay.description: read without a path (READ-011): the nodes of every __overlay__ body, under a root with no properties and no alias.

read-property-entry.description: A property of a merged node, with where its value is set.

read-node.description: A merged node (READ-022, READ-052). A collapsed child has origin base and no properties or children.

read-property.description: One property of a merged node (READ-035), with the binding's description and the suggestions (READ-036).

noos-property-entry.description: Where the backend is noos: a property of a node. $compatible names the node's schema; an external node also has $symbol and $provides (READ-502). source when the property has a value (READ-501).

noos-source.description: Where the backend is noos: who set the value. user for a value the user set or cleared, bootstrap for one bootstrap filled in.

noos-node.description: Where the backend is noos: a node (READ-501). origin is internal for a node the workfile stores, external for a board or driver resource it only names; alias is always empty.

noos-workfile.description: Where the backend is noos: read without a node (READ-500). The root is the workfile: its target (platform, and board when it has one) as properties, the stored nodes as children.

key.description: The workfile's file name without its extension: workfile for workfile.json.

value.description: null for a board when the workfile has none.

noos-property.description: Where the backend is noos: one property (READ-503), with its definition and what it can be set to. suggestions.values are the values update takes; can_create the schemas the user could add instead, [] when none.
